question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the last available daily value of the ICE BofA US High Yield OAS published on the [FRED website](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2) for the final calendar day (typically the final Friday) of the corresponding biweekly period.
question.fine_print:
* If the FRED data is delayed, the value will be taken as soon as published for the relevant date.
* If the market is closed on the scheduled ending date or if no value for that date is published by FRED for two weeks, the most recent available value from an earlier day in the period will be used.
* Only the initially published value for each date will be used (no revisions).
* The value is reported in percentage points.

# HY OAS (BAMLH0A0HYM2): research for the Nov 9-20, 2026 period

The value that counts is FRED's first published print for **Friday, Nov 20, 2026**. The latest value is **3.40 pp on Nov 3**. Nothing has settled the question yet.

  - Oct 1: 3.24.

  - Oct 28: 3.14.

- The question's range of 1.745 to 4.255 is centred near 3.0, which suggests it was set before the latest widening.

[CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/04/investing/us-markets-midterm-elections), [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/business/markets/wall-street-roars-dow-rockets-1500-points-as-democrats-sweep-congress-1.500736418)

  - CCC OAS was 1,307 bps, up more than 500 bps since early September, after peaking at 1,356 bps on Oct 23, its highest in three years.
  - BB was 184 bps and BBB 107 bps, both still around the 8th to 9th percentile of their 20-year ranges.
  - The author says the stress "is not spreading up the ratings ladder." [RIA](https://realinvestmentadvice.com/resources/blog/credit-spreads-calm-on-the-surface-concern-at-the-bottom/)

[Naked Capitalism](https://www.nakedcapitalism.com/2026/11/junk-bond-market-starts-to-crack-in-further-sign-ai-end-game-is-nearing.html)
